# PLAN — ISSUE-288: Bound stalled coordinator Git network operations

Coordinator `fetch`, `push` and `ls-remote` can block forever. When a transport child (ssh, a
ControlPersist master, a proxy) still holds Git's output pipe, `CombinedOutput` keeps waiting for
EOF, even after the context has killed Git. This plan sends those three verbs through one bounded
runner in `internal/gitcredential`. The runner signals **only the Git leader it spawned and has not
yet reaped**. It never signals any transport child, closes its own pipe ends on a fixed budget, and
reports an interrupted push as an **unknown outcome**. Every push site keeps that outcome separate
from conflict, rejection and retry handling. Escaped-descendant cleanup and stronger process
boundaries are out of scope; they belong to draft 294.

Scope is leader-only signaling and bounded owned I/O. No child ownership inference, process-group
signaling, credential/authentication change, new timeout flags or stronger boundary infrastructure.
Issue #294 owns stronger boundaries. REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md contains prior design/test artifacts,
not a separate verdict or lessons section. LESSONS.md is absent; this revision writes only the two
planning artifacts.

## Dimensions
Set by the WorkUnit: size `multi_area`, uncertainty `known`, risk `sensitive`, profile `sensitive`.
No split needed. One new runner (~250 lines), one test-helper package, 14 small call-site edits
and focused tests fit well inside the 16h claim budget.

## What we know
- Every coordinator Git helper uses `exec.CommandContext` plus `CombinedOutput`/`Output` and has no
  network bound: `internal/coordination/store.go:165`, `internal/workspace/worktree.go:635-649`,
  `internal/gitcredential/environment.go:148`, `internal/fork/coordinator.go:703`,
  `internal/lease/checkpoint_reconcile.go:208`. `gitOutput` passes `context.Background()`
  (`worktree.go:636`), so the fetches at `worktree.go:124,295,392` and `recovery.go:51` have no bound at all.
- Go's `exec.Cmd.Wait` (GOROOT `os/exec/exec.go:922-960`) waits for the copy goroutines to reach
  EOF after the process exits. With `WaitDelay`, `ErrWaitDelay` is reported only when the exit was
  otherwise clean ("if err == nil"), so an `ExitError` hides the fact that I/O was still held. A
  runner built on exec's own goroutines therefore cannot tell "known failure, cleanup incomplete"
  apart from "known failure". That is why the plan uses caller-owned `*os.File` pipes.
- `gitcredential.Command` does not set `Setpgid`, and exec's default `Cancel` is
  `Process.Kill` on the leader only. Go 1.26 signals through the pidfd when one is available
  (GOROOT `os/pidfd_linux.go:126`). Either way, an unreaped child's pid cannot be recycled.
- The ten coordination push sites are `store.go:239, 333, 380, 632, 675`, `checkpoints.go:65`,
  `revoke.go:64, 102`, `cleanup.go:48` and `migration.go:102`. Several of them turn *any* push
  error into `ErrConflict` (`cleanup.go:49`, `migration.go:103`, `store.go:334-336` when expected is
  set) or into "no refs changed" (`migration.go:103`). Others re-read the ref and return
  `ErrConflict` when `actual != old` (`store.go:240-246`, `632-638`, `checkpoints.go:66-68`,
  `revoke.go:56-59`). For a push that was interrupted but **landed**, `actual == our commit`, so it
  is misreported as a conflict.
- `lease.Manager.mutate` retries on `ErrConflict` (`internal/lease/manager.go:1152-1172`). Today a
  landed-but-interrupted `CompareAndSwap` therefore re-applies the mutation on top of our own write,
  which is a blind republish. The fork loops `store.go:657-689` and `revoke.go:78-110` `continue` on
  index movement in the same way.
- `manager.go:2036` says "failed without changing either remote ref". That is false for an unknown outcome.
- Callers return publication errors without removing worktrees or branches
  (`workflow/execute_implementation.go:139-149`, `workflow/claim_budget.go:120-140`,
  `pr/service.go:1277-1283`), so the candidate is kept. This plan locks that in with tests.
- Retry already reinspects: `RecordCheckpoint` reloads state, fences on the recorded `HeadSHA`
  (`manager.go:1758-1858`) and pushes with exact `--force-with-lease` leases. `PublishPR` re-reads
  with `ls-remote` and requires `expectedHead` (`workspace/pr.go:522-529`).
- Precedent: `cmd.WaitDelay = time.Second` in `gitcredential/token.go:46` and in the sandbox runners.
- Tools available here: git 2.53.0, `/usr/bin/setsid`, `sh`, `sleep`, Go 1.26.10. These proposed
  files are absent in this snapshot: `internal/gitcredential/network.go`, `network_test.go`,
  `internal/testutil/gittransport/`, `changes/unreleased/288.md`, and the new `_test.go` files listed below. The snapshot has no Git metadata: verify their absence with `git ls-tree -r --name-only <approved-base>` before implementation; if present, modify them instead.

## What we're assuming
- A1: a repo-local `core.sshCommand` plus `ssh.variant=simple` and an `ssh://fake.invalid/<abs>` URL
  drive coordinator Git through the fake transport even under `gitcredential.Configure`. It strips
  only `GIT_CONFIG_*`/`GIT_TRACE*`-class env vars and adds config through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, not
  `core.sshCommand`. Check: step 2's helper self-test runs `gitcredential.Output(..., "ls-remote", url)` in `Pass` mode.
- A2: the remote's `post-receive` hook runs after the ref update when receive-pack is started with
  `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` unset. The coordinator's `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` comes through env and would
  otherwise reach a local receive-pack. Check: the helper self-test asserts `Landed()` and that the remote ref moved.
- A3: `os.Pipe` read ends on Linux are pollable, so `Close` unblocks a pending `Read`. Check: the
  `TestNetworkClosesHeldPipesWithinBudget` reader-exit assertion.
- A4: the 10-minute default network bound does not cut off legitimate coordinator fetches. These
  fetch pinned SHAs or refs, not full clones. It is not user-configurable (no new flags). The
  cheapest check is that existing suites pass unchanged.

## Open questions
- Real OpenSSH ControlMaster/ControlPersist behaviour is not exercised here (no sshd in the
  sandbox). The fake detached holder (step 2) models the documented stderr-holding master. Real-ssh
  verification is a manual follow-up and does not block implementation.
- Leader stuck in uninterruptible sleep (D state) cannot be produced on purpose. It is covered
  through the `waitLeader` seam (step 1); the real kernel case is documented, not reproduced.

## Design

### Step 1 — `internal/gitcredential/network.go` (new)
Exported surface (minimal):
- `var ErrInterrupted = errors.New("git network operation interrupted before Git reported a result")`
- `var ErrCleanupIncomplete = errors.New("git process cleanup incomplete")`
- `func IsNetwork(args []string) bool`: true when `args[0]` is `fetch`, `push` or `ls-remote`.
- `func Network(ctx context.Context, root string, combined bool, args ...string) ([]byte, error)`.
  `KnownResultCleanupError` is exported for caller classification; immutable ExitCode and Operation
  distinguish known success from known failure, and Unwrap preserves causes.
  `combined` gives `CombinedOutput` semantics (one pipe for stdout and stderr). Otherwise stdout is
  returned and stderr is captured on its own pipe into `ExitError.Stderr`, as `cmd.Output()` does.
  The output is raw; callers keep redacting it as they do today.

Unexported budgets and seams (tests in the package override them):
`networkTimeout = 10*time.Minute`, `reapGrace = 5*time.Second`, `ioGrace = 2*time.Second`,
`newPipe = os.Pipe`, `waitLeader = (*exec.Cmd).Wait`; add read/wait injection and completion hooks only for tests. No diagnostic writer or reporting worker.

Sequence:
1. `bctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, networkTimeout)`. An earlier caller deadline wins.
   `defer cancel()`.
2. **Setup paths.** None of these start a process or a worker, and all opened files are closed:
   - (a) `ctx.Err() != nil` → return `fmt.Errorf("git %s not started: %w", op, ctx.Err())`. This is
     **not** `ErrInterrupted`; nothing was sent.
   - (b) `Command(bctx, root, args...)` error (token, config) → return it unchanged.
   - (c) the first or second `newPipe` fails → close every end already opened, then return.
   - (d) `cmd.Start` fails → close all four ends and return a redacted, wrapped start error. Not `ErrInterrupted`.
   - `cmd.Stdin` stays nil (`/dev/null`). Network verbs never take input; the coordination `run`
     with non-empty input on a network verb returns an error.
3. After `Start`, close our copies of the write ends at once. Children hold the only write ends.
4. Workers: one reader goroutine per read end copies into a `bytes.Buffer` (unbounded, as today;
   `ls-remote` output is parsed) and closes `readDone[i]` when it finishes. One waiter goroutine runs
   `waitLeader(cmd)`, stores `ProcessState`/err in the record and closes `reaped`. exec's own ctx
   watcher calls `Process.Kill` (leader only) when `bctx` is done.
5. Orchestration: await `reaped` or cancellation. On cancellation allow at most `reapGrace`
   for the waiter. At that point (or normal reap), establish one absolute cleanup deadline
   `now + ioGrace` shared by ALL readers. Readers still pending at that deadline have their read
   ends closed together; join their pollable reads and close all owned descriptors. Never restart
   grace per reader. No arbitrary writer is invoked, synchronously or from a background goroutine.
6. Classification uses the waiter publication and reader completions, never absent ProcessState:
   - Normal exited leader with exit zero and complete reads: success. Nonzero: preserve
     `*exec.ExitError` with `errors.As`.
   - Normal exited leader with held pipes or any unexpected read error: return a typed
     `KnownResultCleanupError{ExitCode, Operation, ...}` wrapping `ErrCleanupIncomplete`, the
     reader cause and, for nonzero exit, `*exec.ExitError`. Exit zero remains a **known success**,
     including a landed push; it is never `ErrInterrupted` or `ErrPublicationUnknown`. Output is
     explicitly incomplete and cannot be used as a complete fetch/query observation.
   - Signaled leader or no verified exit by reap deadline: `ErrInterrupted`; wrap the context
     cause (DeadlineExceeded/Canceled), or signal ExitError when context is live. Unreaped leader
     also wraps `ErrCleanupIncomplete`.
   - Wait returning unexpected non-ExitError, or returning without ProcessState: conservatively
     `ErrInterrupted` plus `ErrCleanupIncomplete` and the original wait error if any. Never infer
     exit zero or dereference missing state. Reader failures also wrap their cause and cleanup
     sentinel; a verified normal exit remains known even if observation is incomplete.
   - All errors use a redacted message and multi-error unwrap; preserve original typed causes
     behind the wrapper without exposing their unredacted Error text. Interrupted push guidance:
     "remote outcome unknown; rerun the same swarm command to reinspect authoritative state and
     remote head; do not force-push; local candidate retained". Fetch: "no remote refs were
     changed; rerun when reachable". Query: "remote head was not completely observed; rerun".
     Known-success cleanup guidance states "Git completed successfully; cleanup/observation
     incomplete"; for push explicitly say publication is known landed and do not suggest blind retry.
7. **Immutable broadcast and completion.** Readers exclusively own their buffers until closing
   their individual completion channels; copy output into the returned snapshot only after joining
   them. One waiter owns late state/error fields and publishes them by closing `reaped` once.
   Multiple observers wait on closed channels, never consume a one-shot result. The returned
   output/error/cleanup status are independent immutable copies; late reap never changes them.
   One tracked closer closes `settled` only after waiter, all readers, descriptor closures and
   exec cancellation watcher completion (Cmd.Wait joins that watcher) finish. It too has an exit
   acknowledgement for tests. On unexpected Wait/missing-state injection, the seam must still
   perform the real Wait before publishing the injected outcome, so it cannot strand exec workers.
   The intentional unreaped case retains exactly the tracked waiter, exec watcher and completion
   closer until actual Wait returns; readers/descriptors finish before bounded return. Report this
   incomplete cleanup honestly. Tests release late waiters, join the entire run and closer, then
   restore seams. No fire-and-forget reporting or cleanup workers.
8. **Limits (documented in the doc comment).** The return is bounded by roughly
   `min(deadline, 10m) + reapGrace + ioGrace`. These parts are *not* bounded:
   - `cmd.Start` (fork/exec) is synchronous.
   - `GitHubToken` inside `Command` has its own bound (`token.go:46`).
   - A waiter blocked in `wait4` on a D-state leader sits on an OS thread that cannot be
     interrupted. It is leaked until the kernel reaps the leader, and that is reported as cleanup incomplete.
   - `Kill` is a single syscall. Pipe reads go through the netpoller and are interrupted by `Close`.
   - Surviving transports may keep connections open; only pushes without verified leader results are unknown.

`Output` (`environment.go:148`) dispatches to `Network(ctx, root, false, args...)` when
`IsNetwork(args)`. The wrapping stays the same: `fmt.Errorf("git %s: %w", redact(args), err)`.
This covers `lease/cleanup_preview.go:150`, `lease/cleanup.go:121,191`,
`pr/service.go:1242`, `cli/submit_freshness.go:39` and `harness/scaffold.go:159`.
Do not route typed cleanup through any wrapper that labels known landed publication unknown.

### Step 2 — `internal/testutil/gittransport` (new, test-only helper package)
`New(t, bare string) *Transport` writes these files into `t.TempDir()`:
- An `ssh` script. It records `$$` in `clients`, reads the per-service mode file (`upload`,
  `receive`), parses `git-upload-pack '/p'` / `git-receive-pack '/p'` from `$2`, and runs one of:
  - `pass`: run `env -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT git <svc> "$p"` as a child and explicitly wait it
  - `hang`: poll for the `release` file every 50 ms, holding stdio
  - `reject`: print a fixed message to stderr and `exit 128`
  - `land-hang`: like `pass`, but the bare repo's `post-receive` hook writes `landed` and polls for `release`
  - `holder`: start `setsid sh -c '<poll release>' </dev/null >/dev/null &` with stderr inherited,
    record its pid in `master`; a test-owned supervisor waits the holder independently of the SSH adapter, which runs `pass`
- A `post-receive` hook in `bare`.

Methods: `Configure(t, repo, remote)` sets `core.sshCommand`, `ssh.variant=simple` and the
`ssh://fake.invalid<bare>` URL. Also `Set(service, mode)`, `Clients() []int`, `Master() int`,
`Landed() bool`, `Release()` and `Alive(pid) bool` (`kill(pid,0)==nil` and `/proc/<pid>/stat`
state not `Z`). Cleanup is registered before starting any process or making assertions. Test-owned supervisors
start and Wait every child they launch: SSH clients, Git leaders, upload/receive services, hooks,
holders and concurrent clients. Shell supervisors explicitly wait their children; avoid exec/daemon
patterns that orphan test-owned children. Track child birth/exit acknowledgements, including
land-hang post-receive, and join all directly test-owned `exec.Cmd`s with Wait. Survival checks use
Alive, but teardown requires Wait/exit acknowledgements, not merely non-zombie checks.
`Release` is idempotent, releases all modes and injected wait barriers, then joins operations and
supervisors under a bounded teardown watchdog. On watchdog failure record failure first, release
fixtures, join operation and every child, and only then report it. Self-tests exercise this failure
path as well as normal modes. Production never adopts these test process-management mechanisms.

### Step 3 — route coordinator helpers and preserve structured cleanup status
At every helper and publication caller, preserve `KnownResultCleanupError` before generic failure,
conflict or retry mapping. Carry this typed status to the caller without logging to a writer.
Known exit-zero push cleanup returns that explicit known-landed status without re-read/retry,
conflict or unknown classification; known nonzero cleanup retains its exit cause and cleanup status.
Reads with incomplete observations return the structured error instead of parsing partial output.
Audit all dispatch users and the ten push sites below, including higher lease wrappers, for this rule.

Both workspace helper error paths must wrap BOTH `errGitFailed` and the runner error (multiple
`%w` or equivalent multi-unwrap), redacting arguments, normalized diagnostics and displayed cause.
Retain existing push prefixes. `errors.Is` must reach interruption, context and cleanup sentinels,
and `errors.As` must reach ExitError. Do not interpolate a raw underlying error into diagnostics.

### Dispatch touchpoints
- `coordination/store.go:165` `run`: if `gitcredential.IsNetwork(args)`, return an error when input
  is non-empty, otherwise call `Network(ctx, s.root, true, args...)`. Preserve normal diagnostics and redaction, adding typed cleanup handling above.
- `workspace/worktree.go:639` `gitOutputContext`, and through it `gitOutput` at `:635`: use the
  same dispatch. This covers both workspace push callers (`PushForkCheckpointFrom` `:239` and
  `PublishPR` `pr.go:529`) and every workspace fetch/ls-remote.
- `fork/coordinator.go:703` `runGitWithToken` and `lease/checkpoint_reconcile.go:208` `checkpointGit`: same dispatch.

### Step 4 — coordination push sites (all ten)
- Add `var ErrPublicationUnknown = errors.New("coordination publication outcome unknown; reload authoritative state before any retry")` in `store.go`.
- Add `func (s *GitStore) push(ctx context.Context, args ...string) error`. It calls `s.run`; when
  `errors.Is(err, gitcredential.ErrInterrupted)` it returns
  `fmt.Errorf("%w: %w", ErrPublicationUnknown, err)`. It never wraps `ErrConflict`.
- At each site, replace `s.run(ctx, "", push...)` (or `s.git.run`) with `s.push`, then add
  a guard returning unchanged for either `ErrPublicationUnknown` or typed known-result cleanup
  (`"", err`, or `nil, err` for migration). This
  check comes **before** any re-read, `ErrConflict` mapping, "no refs changed" message or loop
  `continue`. Sites: `store.go:239, 333, 380, 632, 675`; `checkpoints.go:65`; `revoke.go:64, 102`;
  `cleanup.go:48`; `migration.go:102`. Ordinary known rejections keep today's mapping; cleanup-bearing failures preserve their extra status.
- `lease/manager.go:2036`: on `errors.Is(err, coordination.ErrPublicationUnknown)`, return
  `fmt.Errorf("atomic PR publication outcome unknown; rerun swarm pr submit %d, which reloads issue state and the PR head before publishing: %w", number, err)`.
  For typed known-result cleanup, preserve explicit known-result guidance instead of the
  "without changing either remote ref" text. Keep ordinary messages otherwise. No lease-policy changes: `mutate` already retries
  only on `ErrConflict`, and `manager.go:1857` maps only `ErrConflict`.

### Step 5 — changelog
- `changes/unreleased/288.md`, one bullet: "Bound coordinator Git fetch, push and ls-remote so
  stalled transports return with retry guidance; interrupted pushes are reported as an unknown
  outcome and never retried blindly."

## HANDOFF
**Entry points**
- `internal/gitcredential/environment.go:148` (`Output` dispatch)
- new `internal/gitcredential/network.go`
- `internal/coordination/store.go:165` (`run`) and the push sites at `store.go:239, 333, 380, 632, 675`, `checkpoints.go:65`, `revoke.go:64, 102`, `cleanup.go:48`, `migration.go:102`
- `internal/workspace/worktree.go:635-649`
- `internal/fork/coordinator.go:703`
- `internal/lease/checkpoint_reconcile.go:208`
- `internal/lease/manager.go:2036`

**Tests and fixtures to extend.** Reuse the setups in these tests; switch the remote to
`gittransport` just before the operation under test:
- coordination: `newRetentionFixture` (`checkpoints_test.go:19`), `newRevokeFixture`
  (`revoke_test.go:24`), the ledger fixture with `seedBranchLedger` (`migration_test.go:24`),
  `TestCleanupAtomicBranchAndStateFences` (`cleanup_test.go:12`),
  `TestForkIndexedStoreAtomicCapAndReplay` (`store_test.go:186`),
  `TestPRPublishRequiresCapturedStateAndRemoteHead` (`store_test.go:99`)
- `TestDroppedCheckpointPublicationFence` (`lease/recovery_publication_test.go:18`)
- `TestPRPublishExactHeadLeaseAndPreservesPrimaryCheckout` (`workspace/pr_test.go:102`)
- `TestPushForkCheckpointFromAllowsOriginOnlyWhenNotUpstream` (`workspace/upstream_remote_test.go:107`)

**Focused commands**
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/gitcredential/... ./internal/testutil/gittransport/...`
- `go test -race -count=1 -run 'Network|Interrupted|Landed|Successor' ./internal/coordination/... ./internal/workspace/... ./internal/lease/... ./internal/fork/...`
- then `make check`

**Assumptions already checked**
- Go's `ErrWaitDelay` masking: read in GOROOT `os/exec/exec.go`.
- pidfd signaling: GOROOT `os/pidfd_linux.go`.
- No `Setpgid` on coordinator Git: `grep -rn Setpgid internal` shows only `process/tree_unix.go`, which coordinator Git does not use.
- No test asserts the push error messages being changed: grep of each message string under `internal`, `cmd` and `docs` returned none.
- Proposed new files are absent in this snapshot; approved-base verification remains an implementation preflight because Git metadata is unavailable here.

**Reopen the plan instead of widening the change if:**
- A1 or A2 fails and the fake transport needs env or credential changes in `Configure`.
- Any site needs in-process reinspection or retry to pass.
- A test seems to require signaling a transport child.
- `networkTimeout` breaks an existing suite.
- Non-network Git verbs appear to need the runner.

**What this change breaks** (from greps)
- The push error text for *interrupted* pushes changes at the 10 sites. No test asserts these strings.
- `manager.go:2036` text changes only for the unknown outcome.
- Known-rejection messages and `ErrConflict` mapping are unchanged, including `migration_test.go:230`,
  `revoke_test.go:238`, `cleanup_test.go:12` and `store_test.go:16, 99`.
- `TestConcurrentIssueReadsStayPinnedAndTransportErrorsSurface` (`store_test.go:150`) is unchanged:
  ordinary transport errors stay known failures.
- `docs/fork-mode.md:61` (client timeout re-query) is unaffected and preserved unchanged.
- No CLI flags or docs are added.
- Error values that used to be a bare `*exec.ExitError` stay matchable with `errors.As`.

**Recommended follow-ups (not in this WorkUnit)**
- `PushForkCheckpointFrom` leases on a freshly observed fork head (`worktree.go:226-239`), so a
  retry can replace another writer on that claim-scoped fork branch. Consider fencing it on the
  recorded head.
- Real OpenSSH ControlMaster verification.
- Stronger process boundary (draft 294).

## Operator guidance

> Resolve exactly the five latest review findings; the revised scope and leader-only safe policy are accepted. (1) Workspace helper must wrap BOTH existing errGitFailed sentinel and underlying typed runner error with redaction; tests both push callers plus read. (2) Never synchronously write cleanup warnings to arbitrary writer or spawn untracked writer goroutine; carry structured known-result cleanup status through callers with bounded return and a single shared deadline. Known landed push is not unknown. (3) Specify unexpected Wait/missing ProcessState/reader errors, every started-run path and immutable broadcast results; explicit whole worker/descriptor completion on all paths with restored seams only afterward. (4) Make old/new runtime proof compile on old tree: baseline-compatible caller-level or legacy Command+CombinedOutput harness, watchdog always releases fixture then joins operation before reporting failure, track/Wait all test-owned hooks/git/services as well as ssh, cleanup registered before any assertions. (5) Add PublishPR landed interruption plus successor expected-head refusal and candidate retention, no new semantics. Correct empty-evidence/LESSONS existence claims. Keep concise self-contained design/test definitions, no obsolete revision references or broader cleanup. No product edits during plan.

# TEST_PLAN — ISSUE-288

Every test is self-contained (the legacy harness described below embeds its own fixture). It builds its own temporary bare remote and clone with `gitfixture`,
drives coordinator Git through `internal/testutil/gittransport` (PLAN step 2), and releases its own
fixture processes; `gittransport`'s `t.Cleanup` verifies their completed waits and exit acknowledgements.

**Baseline runtime proof (separate from new-API tests).** Add a self-contained test file
`internal/gitcredential/network_legacy_regression_test.go` with no dependency on Network, new
sentinels or the new transport package. It creates its own shell fixture and uses only the existing
`Command(ctx, root, args...)` plus `cmd.CombinedOutput()` for the legacy branch; on the fixed tree
it exercises the existing exported `Output` caller. Select the legacy branch with a test-only
`SWARM_TEST_LEGACY_GIT=1` environment variable. Test name:
`TestLegacyCompatibleNetworkBound/{fetch,push,ls-remote}`. Use a short caller deadline, a
release-file holder that keeps inherited output open, and an outer 8s watchdog. The assertion is
bounded return within caller deadline + 5s reap + 2s I/O + slack on fixed Output (use a longer
outer watchdog there, 20s). Legacy completion remains blocked beyond context cancellation and
fails the independent 8s watchdog at runtime, then is released and joined. This harness tests the
old helper unchanged; it does not pretend new-API tests compile on the base.

Reproduction, after implementation, in two disposable checkouts outside the protected tree:
```
# Copy ONLY the self-contained legacy regression test to the approved-base checkout.
cd "$ISSUE288_BASE_CHECKOUT"
SWARM_TEST_LEGACY_GIT=1 go test -count=1 -timeout=60s -run '^TestLegacyCompatibleNetworkBound$' ./internal/gitcredential
# Expected runtime failure: watchdog records unbounded CombinedOutput, not a compile failure.
cd "$ISSUE288_FIXED_CHECKOUT"
go test -count=1 -timeout=90s -run '^TestLegacyCompatibleNetworkBound$' ./internal/gitcredential
```
Record the approved base SHA, fixed SHA, copy command, exact output and elapsed bounds in
validation evidence. These checkouts/commands are implementation work, not performed in planning.

**Unconditional teardown contract.** Register cleanup before assertions or child Start. Every
watchdog first records the failure, releases fixtures AND blocked wait seams, then boundedly joins
the operation goroutine and all worker/child completions before reporting via Error/Fatal. Never
Fatal before release. Every directly test-owned Git, SSH, supervisor, service, hook and holder has
one Wait owner; supervisors explicitly wait their own children and report completion. Cleanup
checks descriptor closure and child completion acknowledgements, not only Alive/PID disappearance.
The fixture self-test intentionally triggers early assertion failure and watchdog paths via a
nonfatal recording test facade and proves release/join ran. If bounded join itself fails, report
that separate teardown failure after attempting fixture termination and final Wait. T8 installs
its release/join cleanup before invoking Network and restores seams only after complete settlement.

Cross-package tests use a caller context deadline of 5 s. They cannot shrink the unexported
budgets, so their bound is 5 + 5 + 2 + 3 = 15 s. In-package `gitcredential` tests set
`networkTimeout = 300ms`, `reapGrace = 1s` and `ioGrace = 300ms`.

**Shorthand used below**
- **"Classified interrupted"** means:
  - `errors.Is(err, gitcredential.ErrInterrupted)` is true;
  - `errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)` is true, or `context.Canceled` where stated;
  - the error message contains the operation-specific guidance from PLAN step 1.6;
  - the error message contains no token, `basic `, or absolute temp path.
- **"Survivors"** means:
  - every pid in `Clients()` and `Master()` is still `Alive` right after the call returns, so they were never signaled;
  - a test-started unrelated `sleep 60` (via `exec.Command`, in the test's own process group) is `Alive`;
  - the test kills that `sleep` itself in cleanup.

## Acceptance criterion 1
> Hanging-transport regressions fail against the old behaviour and show bounded return, effective cancellation, a retained candidate and safe operation-specific retry guidance. Git and owned I/O stop within the budget, and unresolved child cleanup is reported explicitly. Shared direct or detached SSH masters, concurrent clients and unrelated processes survive. Any child that is signaled has independent proof of exclusive ownership and a verified exit.

All tests in this group are in `internal/gitcredential/network_test.go` (new) unless a file is named.

# Implementation — ISSUE-288

Implemented the approved leader-only network runner and publication classifications. Fetch,
push and ls-remote have a 10 minute default bound (an earlier caller deadline wins), a 5 second
leader-reap grace and one shared 2 second I/O cleanup deadline. Only exec's unreaped Git leader
is signaled. Held transport descriptors are closed locally; ambiguous/direct/shared transports
survive with explicit incomplete-cleanup status. No transport child ownership inference, process
group signaling, credentials/authentication changes, flags, cgroups or progress-policy changes.

The waiter and readers publish through closed broadcast channels. The tracked settlement worker
waits for the waiter exit and all descriptor-owning reader exits; its own completion is acknowledged.
Returned output and errors are snapshots. A delayed Wait retains the tracked completion workers
until released; it cannot change the returned result. No production warning writer or reporting
worker exists. Normal Git exit plus incomplete observation produces KnownResultCleanupError;
exit-zero push says publication is known landed. Unverified/signaled exit produces ErrInterrupted,
preserving context and typed causes behind sanitized diagnostics.

All ten coordination push sites guard unknown publication and typed known-result cleanup before
conflict mapping, rereading or retrying. Interrupted publication wraps ErrPublicationUnknown.
CompletePRRevision gives authoritative-state/head reinspection guidance. Workspace failures expose
both errGitFailed and the underlying typed cause while displaying sanitized diagnostics. Existing
expected-head and fork checkpoint lease policies are preserved.

Owned changelog fragment: changes/unreleased/288.md (one bullet).

| Setup and exceptional paths | `TestNetworkSetupPaths`: pre-canceled context, first/second pipe failure, Start failure, closed created descriptors and no transport invocation. `TestNetworkTokenSetupFailure` and `TestNetworkRejectsInput` cover credential setup and unsupported input. `TestNetworkExceptionalObservation`, `TestNetworkReadErrorsOnEachPipe`, and completion table cover each output pipe, combined/separate streams, cancellation, unexpected Wait, missing ProcessState and late Wait. |
| Causes, typed errors and redaction | Ordinary fetch/push/query failures retain `*exec.ExitError`; interruption preserves context cancellation/deadline and ErrInterrupted. Read/Wait injected causes remain reachable. Known-result cleanup preserves `KnownResultCleanupError`, ErrCleanupIncomplete and ExitError for failure. Every row sees one receive attempt; unknown outcomes avoid ErrConflict and misleading rejection/no-change text. Held-I/O normal success remains typed known landed; known nonzero exit remains known failure with cleanup status. Source inspection confirms guards precede reinspection/conflict/loop handling at all ten sites. Both workspace push callers preserve known-landed cleanup. No diagnostic writer or reporting goroutine exists in the runner API. |
| Authoritative retry/CAS/head fences | `TestInterruptedCASRetryReinspects` covers landed, not-landed and successor outcomes: fresh Load observes authoritative state; stale expected revision conflicts and leaves winner unchanged; unchanged state permits normal retry. `TestMutateDoesNotRetryUnknownPublication` verifies one receive and one authoritative renewal. `TestRecordCheckpointLandedThenRetry` verifies retained candidate, one subsequent state commit and successor claim fencing. `TestPublishPRLandedInterruptionAndSuccessor` captures E/C, independently observes landed C or successor S, retries with E, verifies zero additional receives and preserves winner/candidate/branch/worktree. Source preserves known cleanup before that generic message. `changes/unreleased/288.md` exists with the scoped changelog entry. |

## Remaining evidence gaps

1. **Approved-base runtime comparison:** unavailable Git metadata prevents the exact two-checkout/SHA proof required by the test plan. The independently observed legacy runtime failures above are useful bounded-return regression evidence, but do not establish baseline provenance or prove existing adversarial test files are unchanged.
2. **Exhaustive teardown/error-path coverage:** `TestTransportTeardownPaths` at `internal/testutil/gittransport/transport_test.go:71` has three scenario labels, but all execute the same legacy watchdog path. “Early assertion” merely invokes a recording callback before starting the operation; “blocked waiter” has no distinct injected Wait barrier. It does not inject setup failure after each child Start as promised by TEST_PLAN.md. Normal fixture teardown and actual watchdog cleanup pass, but these passing rows do not establish every planned failure path.
3. **Per-row lifetime accounting:** whole-run tests establish settlement/read-descriptor/reap completion across important exceptional outcomes. The isolated fd-count and captured-all-pipe-end assertions occur in the held-pipe test, not every T23/setup row. Missing-state rows wait settlement but do not call assertSettled. Therefore the strongest test-plan claim of complete per-row descriptor/worker accounting is only partially established. Source inspection supports the cleanup design; it cannot substitute for the missing adversarial coverage.

Real OpenSSH ControlMaster/ControlPersist and kernel D-state behavior remain explicitly untested environment limits from the approved plan. Deterministic detached holders and delayed-Wait seams cover their scoped models. Descendant cleanup beyond the owned leader is issue #294; surviving ambiguous processes are reported as incomplete cleanup, never silently represented as complete.

AC1: observed bounded-return, survivor, guidance and retention behavior passes; exact baseline-checkout traceability remains unverified. AC2: observed typed/error/retry/fence behavior passes; exhaustive teardown-path acceptance remains incomplete pending the coverage above; `make check` passed. No code changes were made to conceal these gaps.
